queue.recognise: You can recognise it by the black park sign in front of it naming it the Giant Tree, national champion coast redwood. It stands on the Big Trees Loop by the Big Tree Area parking on Bull Creek.
queue.story:
In November 1991 the American Forestry Association named this coast redwood the national champion of its species, and the park's sign beside it still gives the figures. It is 363 feet tall, about 110 metres, with a trunk 53.2 feet round, about 16 metres, and an average crown spread of 62 feet. Save the Redwoods League explains that the title goes to the best combination of height, trunk and crown, not to height alone.

queue.name: The Giant Tree

queue.recognise: You can recognise it by the wooden sign at its foot reading Tall Tree, measured February 1957. It stands on Bull Creek Flat in Rockefeller Forest, in the same grove as the Giant Tree.
queue.story:
When this coast redwood was measured in February 1957 it stood 359.3 feet tall, about 109.5 metres, and the sign the park put beside it still says so. The same sign gives a trunk 42 feet round at breast height, almost 13 metres, and 13.4 feet across. Redwood writers call it the Rockefeller Tall Tree and say it once held the title of the world's tallest known tree, a title it has long since lost.

It grows on Bull Creek Flat in Rockefeller Forest, part of Humboldt Redwoods State Park, which holds the largest remaining continuous old-growth coast redwood forest in the world. queue.recognise: A huge dark cedar with several trunks rising inside a low fence, information boards and a white bench with a red heart in front of it on the lawn.
queue.story:
Italy keeps a national register of its monumental trees, and Varese, the garden city at the foot of the Alps between Lake Maggiore and Lake Como, has several. A reader sent us this one, and the register lists a Lebanon cedar here, 34 metres tall.

The photograph shows a tree that has outgrown its garden. Several trunks rise together from the lawn and carry a dark, tiered crown so broad that it fills the frame from side to side, the layered branches stepping out in the flat shelves that make a cedar of Lebanon recognisable from far away. queue.name: Cedar of Lebanon in Varese
